## Teaching points

1. Severe magnesium depletion can cause cramps, refractory hypokalemia and ventricular arrhythmia. Replace magnesium and monitor rhythm and potassium.
2. Replace magnesium under monitoring and address accompanying hypokalemia and hypocalcemia; review diuretic and PPI use.
3. Magnesium and potassium are static laboratory values in this case because the engine cannot link them to replacement. Repeat testing is still part of the clinical plan; no automatic normalization is implied.
